title: I have two sisters
goal: Say what you have and don't have with a possessive and bar or ýok, and ask with barmy.

intro.text: To say **I have**, put the possessive on the thing and add *bar*: *Meniň doganym bar*. **I don't have**: *ýok*. Ask with *barmy?*: *Jigiň barmy?* After a number the noun stays singular: *iki doganym*.

exercises.label: *dogan* + *bar*: I have a brother or sister, you have…
exercises.explain: The possessive ending changes with the person; *bar* stays the same.

reject.why: After a number the noun stays singular: *iki gyzym*.
Turkmen has no verb **to have**: put **my** on the noun and add *bar*: *iki gyzym bar*.
**My** is an ending on the noun: *gyzym*.

exercises.question: How do you say **I don't have time**?

why.1: **Have** is the possessive on the noun with *bar* or *ýok*: *wagtym ýok*.
why.2: *däl* says what something **is not**. Not having is *ýok*.

exercises.explain: *wagt* + *-ym* (my time) + *ýok* (doesn't exist): I have no time.

exercises.text: Jigi___ barmy? — Hawa, bir jigim bar.
exercises.en: Do you have a younger brother or sister? — Yes, I have one.

reject.why: *jigim* is **my** younger sibling. The question asks about **yours**: *jigiň*.

exercises.explain: *jigi* ends in a vowel: **your** is *-ň*: *jigiň barmy?*

exercises.question: How many older sisters does Arslan have?

context.en: Arslan, do you have brothers or sisters?

context.tk: Hawa, meniň bir agam we iki uýam bar. Jigim ýok.

why.1: He has **one** older brother, *bir agam*, and **two** older sisters, *iki uýam*.
why.2: *Jigim ýok*: it's a younger brother or sister he doesn't have.

exercises.explain: *iki uýam bar*: I have two older sisters.

exercises.prompt: Do you have a pen? (to a friend)
exercises.explain: Both work: *Sende ruçka barmy?* asks whether there's one on you now, *Ruçkaň barmy?* whether you own one.

exercises.question: Someone asks *Wagtyň barmy?* You do. What do you answer?

why.1: That says **yes, my time**. The short answer repeats *bar*.
why.2: *Men bar* would say **I exist**. Repeat just *bar*.

exercises.explain: The short answer repeats the word of the question: *bar* or *ýok*.
After a number the noun stays singular, with **my** on it: *üç çagam*.

exercises.prompt: Iki jigim we bir uýam bar.
accept: I have two younger siblings and an older sister.
I have two younger [brothers|sisters] and [an|one] older sister.
I have two younger siblings and one older sister.
I have two younger brothers or sisters and [an|one] older sister.
exercises.explain: *jigi* is a younger brother or sister, *uýa* an older sister; *-m* is **my**, and *bar* says they exist.
